newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan-China trade slips 2.4 pct in January.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan-China trade slips 2.4 pct in January.

text.p: Taiwan's trade with arch rival China slid 2.4 percent to US$1.967 billion in January from January 1996, the Board of Foreign Trade said on Thursday.

Taiwan's trade with China -- routed indirectly through Hong Kong to skirt Taipei's 48-year-old ban on direct mainland trade -- represented about 10 percent of the island's total foreign trade, a board statement said.
Exports to China totalled US$1.627 billion in January, down 3.7 percent from a January 1996, accounting for 15.8 percent of Taiwan's total exports.
Imports from China hit a record $340 million in January, up 4.5 percent year on year and accounting for 3.7 percent of total imports.
The board attributed the export decline to decreasing mainland imports of car parts and textile products.
Taiwan's steady growth in export orders and industrial output have boosted demand for imports of semi-finished goods and raw material from the mainland, the board said.
In January, Taiwan enjoyed a $1.287 billion trade surplus with China, down 5.7 percent from January 1996.
Communist China and Nationalist-ruled Taiwan have been rivals since a civil war split them in 1949.
More than 30,000 Taiwan firms have operations in the Chinese mainland with investment totalling more than $20 billion since political tensions started to ease in the late 1980s.
